newsitem.title: UK: All NATO states to decide who will join - Britain.
newsitem.headline: All NATO states to decide who will join - Britain.

text.p: Britain said on Thursday the U.S. decision to push for the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland to join NATO would contribute to the debate on expanding the alliance but the final decision would be taken by all 16 members of the defence group.
U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen announced the decision to support the three nations and to exclude Romania and Slovenia in the first wave at a NATO defence ministers' meeting in Brussels.
A U.S. spokesman insisted Washington would stand by its decision and did not want to be overruled by other members at the NATO summit in Madrid in July.
"The U.S. contribution is obviously an important contribution to the debate," a spokesman for the British Foreign Office told Reuters.

"The decision on who to invite will be taken by all 16 members together over the next weeks leading to Madrid and the allies will discuss with the secretary general, bilaterally and all together the decisions which we must take in Madrid," he added.
The decision to expand the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation has been on the cards since 1994, despite opposition by Russia which reversed its stand this spring.
Hungarian, Polish and Czech officials welcomed the U.S. decision, but Romania and Slovenia have insisted that they would continue to push Washington to back them.
Some other European members, most notably Italy and Germany, have supported Romanian membership.
Britain has remained coy about its choices and would not be pushed further to comment on the U.S. decision.
But the United States is the dominant member of the alliance and along with Germany pays for more than 50 percent of its costs.
